minor.issue: evidence field is wrapped in matching double quotes. HzJr0Bjq returns evidence='"George Orwell's '1984' is supposed to be a warning, NOT an instruction manual."' (also visible in the UI 'EVIDENCE › ""…""'). Spec explicitly says 'evidence NOT wrapped in quote characters'. Fix in generator.py normalize_payload: strip surrounding smart/straight quotes from evidence after _clamp (e.g. evidence = re.sub(r'^["“‘\']+|["”’\']+$', '', _clamp(...))).

issues: Evidence renders as double-wrapped quotes '""…""' because backend evidence is already wrapped in '"…"' and the UI adds its own quote styling. Fix after backend quote-stripping lands.

action_items: Strip surrounding quote characters from evidence in generator.normalize_payload (both regular and smart quotes). Example on HzJr0Bjq: '"George Orwell\'s \'1984\' …manual."' → 'George Orwell\'s \'1984\' …manual.'

critical_code_review_comments: generator.normalize_payload clamps 'evidence' but never trims wrapping quotes. The writer prompt instructs 'verbatim or lightly trimmed quote' — Claude is returning the quote wrapped in '"…"' which is passing straight through. Add quote-strip step.

server.episode_card returns 404 when image_status != 'ready'; the fallback test depended on the old episodes still being image-ready. If an old episode has image_status in {pending,failed}, GET /card will 404 instead of serving the still. Consider serving the raw still even when image_status != 'ready' as long as image_path exists, so old items never 404 just because their status field was never set.

HzJr0Bjq remains the stable regression episode (spice=savage, cast=[Homer, Marge, Kent Brockman, Mr. Burns], still_kind=likeness, card 1080x1350).
rca of the issue: evidence quote-wrap: Claude 3.5 Haiku frequently returns the 'evidence' JSON string already wrapped in double quotes to signal 'this is a quote from the user' (e.g. "\"George Orwell's '1984'…manual.\""). generator.normalize_payload calls _clamp which only trims whitespace+length and converts to str — it does NOT strip wrapping quotes. The field is then persisted and surfaced as-is through ep_public, so both the API payload and the UI (which wraps evidence inside its own typographic quotes in EpisodeCard) end up double-quoted. Fix is a one-liner in normalize_payload: evidence = re.sub(r'^["\u201c\u2018\'`]+|["\u201d\u2019\'`]+$', '', _clamp(data.get('evidence'), 110)).strip().
